narrative: Burbage gives the crown away with his own hands. He washes off his own balm. The three leaves are the ones no public house has heard. The floor is still the six paces. The chair has not changed its mind by moving. He sends for the glass. He looks. He dashes it on Sir Edward's boards. The glass is four shillings. It is the first time, and it is the only time. No one at the table stirs. The pieces stay where they fell. The table is a table. Twelve faces, and not one of them leans in to ask. Sir Robert does not move. The stool behind the screen does not produce a comment. The parliament has been heard, and the room has not become a council.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Stood in the scene, and did not prompt the table.

entities.name: Richard Burbage
entities.context: Gave the crown with his own hands, and dashed the glass.

entities.name: Sir Robert Cecil
entities.context: Did not move when the glass broke.

entities.name: Sir Edward Hoby
entities.context: Had his boards dashed, and did not rise to them.
